column1: # The review set's coverage contract. Tab-separated, `#` for comments.
# WHAT THIS IS. `tools/review-shots.mjs` writes the frames a vision reviewer
# judges, and `tools/verify_shots.py` decides whether that set is worth
# reviewing. Until r171 the gate asked "is this a real render from a played
# bout?" and never "is every state still here?".
# It could not ask. `MIN_FRAMES = 8` is a floor on a *count*, so a set missing
# the paused overlay, the fighter pick, the half-point score and the kick at
# range — sixteen of twenty-four frames — still exits 0. Three captures have a
# guard that `return`s without writing a file (22, 23 and the r169 settings
# capture all do), so that is not a hypothetical: the tool is built to skip a
# frame quietly, and the gate cannot see it happen.
# That is r158's sentence applied to the loop's own primary instrument. A state
# that becomes reachable is not a state that has been reviewed — and here the
# states a reviewer is shown are chosen by a file nobody diffs against a list of
# what the game can show.
# HOW IT IS ENFORCED, in two halves, because there are two different failures:
#   `apps/game/tests/unit/review-set-covers-declared-frames.test.ts`  (offline,
#     in `pnpm check`) reads `review-shots.mjs` and asserts both directions —
#     every capture is declared here and every declaration is a capture. That
#     catches the AUTHOR: a new capture added without a row.
#   `tools/verify_shots.py --frames` reads this file against the set on disk and
#     fails on a declared frame that was not written. That catches the RUN: a
#     capture whose guard bailed, a browser that died mid-run, a stale
#     frame left over from a previous set.
# THE `kind` COLUMN, and it is not decoration. A capture that photographs a
# guaranteed screen is `capture`. A capture that photographs a MOMENT — a kick
# at contact, a half on the board — can legitimately fail to find its subject,
# and its own guard `return`s without writing a file. Those are `opportunistic`
# and the gate reports a missing one as UNCOVERED rather than as a failure.
# There is **one `opportunistic` row fewer**, down from three to two, and each
# row that changed changed for a measured reason rather than a policy one.
# r171 recorded the debt: their guards fired 10, 8 and 8 times across the
# retained loop logs and nothing noticed, and four review passes had argued about
# the half-point notation on sets where — as it turned out — **the half point was
# in none of them.** r172 went and measured all three. Every number below was read
# off a clock or a pixel on this machine before anything was changed.
#   19  THE HALF — was dead, not unlucky. Its observer polled
#       `.points .score-frac`, an element **r148 deleted** when it made the half a
#       single text node; `styles.css:863` says there is deliberately no such rule
#       and `score-notation.test.ts:116` is a tripwire against one returning. So it
#       latched zero times in every run since r148 shipped, and "8 firings" was an
#       undercount of a total failure. Now it reads the `½` glyph in the score's
#       own text, before and after the shutter. Reliable for a structural reason:
#       **a half stays on the board until the next point**, so its subject does not
#       expire in four ticks. Measured 3/3, throw 6 every time.
#   18  THE KICK AT CONTACT — much better, and **still `opportunistic`, because
#       "much better" is not "reliable" and the difference is the load.** A landed
#       kick awards a call, and the referee phase holds the striker on the pose's
#       `contact` frame for 96 ticks (`spriteFrames.ts`), so the SIM holds the pose
#       for about a second and a half — which is a real structural handle, and it
#       took this capture from 0 kept shutters in 12 throws to landing on throw 1.
#       Measured **4/4 correct at load 7.0-11.7** (`cell 64 active -> active`, and
#       the kept frames were looked at: leg up, foot on the defender's body).
#       Then at **load 16.2** the same capture reported `cell 64 active -> active`
#       and photographed **both fighters standing in guard**. That is the
#       compositor presenting a frame older than the referee's own hold, and no
#       amount of reading `spriteFrames()` either side of the shutter can see it,
#       because both reads agree with each other and both disagree with the
#       picture. Standing rule 5: a measurement that cannot be reproduced is not a
#       result. Four greens at load 7-11 and one red at 16 is not a reliable
#       capture, it is a capture that works when the machine is quiet — and this
#       machine does not idle, which is r151's standing warning and the reason a
#       frequency check is not a gate.
#   21  THE KICK INTO OPEN AIR — **still opportunistic, and the reason is
#       hardware rather than carelessness.** A whiffed kick gets no call and so no
#       referee hold, so its subject is a 26-tick transient. A screenshot costs
#       more than that: measured in simulation ticks, playwright clip PNG **26**,
#       jpeg q50 **15**, CDP `optimizeForSpeed` 19, full frame 25. So the probe
#       shutter is jpeg now, which is the difference between impossible and a coin
#       flip — it landed on throws 3, 5, 7, 8, 10 and 17 across the runs, against
#       roughly one set in six before. But the sandwich is necessary and not
#       sufficient: the compositor presents a frame later than the sim advances, so
#       a capture bracketed by `active` and `recovery` can still return a guard
#       stance. **The kept frame was looked at and it was a guard stance.**
#       Flipping this row to `capture` would make the gate permanently red, and a
#       gate that cries wolf gets deleted.
# Two designs were built and measured out before the one that shipped, and both
# are worth the ink because each looked certain:
#   FREEZING THE PAGE ON THE FRAME. Returning 0 from `requestAnimationFrame` at
#   the latch leaves the page producing no further compositor frame, so
#   `Page.captureScreenshot` hands back the last cached surface: after the freeze a
#   magenta timer and a 12px green body outline **do not appear either**, and the
#   fighters' box came back byte-identical to an idle reference. This is how a
#   guard stance nearly got filed as "the renderer draws no kick". The renderer is
#   fine — atlas cells 61..66 are a front kick, and a live screenshot taken while
#   the rig reported cell 61 photographs a leg up.
#   CHECKING THE PIXELS FOR A POSE. A kick moves the CAMERA — it is the only move
#   the camera pulls back for — and the camera's response is not a pose. Measured
#   with the fighter back in its guard, cell 0, 1200ms after the strike finished:
#   delta **4.04 / 4.44 / 4.42 / 5.02 / 5.81**, against an idle-vs-idle floor of
#   **0.34**. No threshold separates them. With one set at 3 this gate passed a
#   frame in which both fighters were standing in guard, which is how it was
#   caught. A gate that cannot fail is worse than one that cannot run, so it is
#   gone rather than re-tuned.
# What replaced the honest half is not nothing: `review-shots.mjs` exits **1** when
# it fails to deliver a DECLARED `capture`, so the capture says so at the moment
# it happens rather than leaving a tally for a gate to find later. And it reads the
# kinds from THIS file rather than a second list, because two lists is two things
# to forget to update.
# Proved able to fail in `tools/verify-shots-mutation.sh`.
# ADDING A ROW is not enough on its own — the same rule `tools/art-manifest.tsv`
# carries. A capture that is not photographed is not declared, and a declaration
# the gate enforces but the tool never writes is a red gate, not a covered state.
# name

column1: 18-phone-kick
column4: r89's 2.96:1 foot, the measurement that drives open item 2.1. r172 found the structural handle — a LANDED kick awards a call and the referee phase holds the striker on the contact frame for 96 ticks — and took this capture from 0 kept shutters in 12 throws to landing on throw 1: 4/4 correct at load 7.0-11.7, frames looked at. But at load 16.2 it reported `cell 64 active -> active` and photographed a guard stance, so it stays `opportunistic`. Was missing from roughly one set in six

column1: 19-phone-half-point
column4: r148's typography, and the set's most-missed frame: it was watching for a `.score-frac` element r148 had itself deleted, so it had a 0% hit rate in every run since. It reads the `½` glyph in the score's own text now, before and after the shutter. **The one capture here that is genuinely reliable**, for a structural reason: a half STAYS on the board until the next point, so its subject does not expire in four ticks. Measured 5/5 across load 7.0-16.2, throw 6 every time, and every kept frame looked at. The geometry is gated deterministically by tools/scoreline-stability.mjs regardless

column1: 21-phone-kick-open
column3: a kick thrown into open air, whole end to end
column4: the frame that settles the "amputated kick" family of six reviews — a landed kick puts the foot on the defender's body under an impact effect, obscuring the very thing being judged. Rebuilt at r172 with a jpeg probe shutter (26 ticks to 15, measured) and 30 throws, which took it from about one set in six to a coin flip. It stays `opportunistic` because a whiffed kick gets no referee hold and the compositor presents later than the sim advances: a capture bracketed `active -> recovery` was looked at and came back a guard stance. Its row used to say "a kick landing on the defender's body", which is the one thing this capture exists to avoid
